title: impl(pm-stack): browser-dependent quota watchdog core — disk state, failure classes, repair ladder

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

body:
Implements the watchdog core from the design in #6031 (browser-dependent quota watchdog). Scope is the **generic** machinery only — no provider specifics; Mistral is adapter #1 on top of this (openchamber issue, linked from #6031).

## What to build

In `pm-stack` (this repo), deployed on the laptop beside the gatherer:

1. **Watchdog oneshot + timer** (`pm-stack/systemd/`): runs on the gatherer's 15-minute rhythm, offset (e.g. `*:3/15`) so it judges fresh producer documents. Oneshot discipline like the existing laptop watchdog family (laptop-backups-watchdog code#1841, codex-remote-control-watchdog code#1845).
2. **State file** `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-state.json` — atomic tmp+rename writes; per-source health record: `lastAttemptAt`, `lastSuccessAt`, `consecutiveFailures`, `currentClass`, sanitized `lastDetail`, `cooldownUntil`, `repairLog` (last 20), `incident` refs. **Nothing decision-relevant lives in process memory** — this is code#5928's lesson applied from day one (cross-tick cooldown + failure counts on disk).
3. **Failure-class evaluation:** read each registered source's `~/atlas/<provider>-export/latest.json` + the gatherer heartbeat; classify into `session-expired` / `cookie-missing` / `endpoint-changed` / `browser-down` / `cdp-unreachable` / `rate-limited` / `unknown` (producer pre-classifies its own failures; the watchdog owns classes the producer cannot see, e.g. missing document, browser process state).
4. **Repair ladder executor** with per-rung attempt caps (max 2 per incident) and a persisted repair log, cheapest first: (0) rate-limit cooldown honored from disk; (1) retry next tick (no-op rung); (2) CDP session re-validation against the live laptop browser (cookie **presence by name**; in-page fetch re-run — the cookie value is not read into the process; extraction only for adapters that declare a header-token path, value → fleet secrets by registered name only); (3) browser re-login driver via the provider's own SSO flow using the browser's standing Google session — stops dead at a human-only challenge and marks the incident **human-blocked**. Rung 4 (escalation) is the sibling escalation issue, invoked from here.
5. **Adapter loader:** read per-provider adapter files (`pm-stack/exporters/adapters/`) — origins allowlist, CDP port, data-path order, cookie names, login hints, class map, thresholds. The core contains zero provider names.
6. **Producer scaffolding:** a forkable producer template from the retired Meta producer (`~/atlas/meta-quota-export/meta-quota-export.mjs` on the laptop — CDP plumbing, tab ownership per code#5121, per-call timeouts, failure-class exit codes, atomic latest.json + history.jsonl), landing producer source in `pm-stack/exporters/`; plus the gatherer `FILE_EXPORTS` registration step documented/wired for each adopted source.
7. **Health history:** append per-tick per-source observations to `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-watchdog-history.jsonl` (interim); emit into the usage snapshot pipeline once code#4889's laptop path bug is fixed (do not block on it).

## Safety bounds (from the design)

Never writes quota data; never changes credentials other than re-storing an extracted session under its registered secret name; browser automation only against adapter allowlist origins, read endpoints + login flow only; no secret value in any log, state field, or document; login attempt caps double as account-lockout protection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Watchdog oneshot + timer installed on the laptop and ticking on the gatherer cadence; state file written atomically each tick and surviving across invocations (demonstrated over ≥3 consecutive ticks).
- [ ] A synthetic broken source (fixture adapter + producer stub) walks the ladder: retry → CDP re-validation → re-login attempt → escalation hand-off, with each rung's attempt recorded in `repairLog` and caps honored (no rung attempted >2× per incident).
- [ ] A `rate-limited` fixture sets `cooldownUntil` on disk and the next tick honors it without any browser action (the #5928 regression test, in effect).
- [ ] Human-only challenge fixture marks the incident human-blocked and the state carries the surfacing flag the orchestration/stewardship sweeps read.
- [ ] Quiet when healthy: a healthy source produces no output beyond journal/state/history records.
- [ ] Tests name their oracles per the testing doctrine (state-machine invariants for the ladder are a natural PBT/MBT fit).

Related: #6031 (design), #1260 (self-healing umbrella), #5928 (cross-tick state), #4889 (snapshot history path).
